Hong Kong Open 2026: Emotional Alexandra Eala stunned by Claire Liu in final
 Second seed Eala was stunned 6-3, 6-0 by Liu in the summit clash as the American ranked 102 won her first tour title.
 Updated : Nov 08, 2026 18:04 IST , Hong Kong - 2 MINS READ

 Claire Liu of the US (left) holds up the winner's trophy with Philippines' Alexandra Eala after their Hong Kong Open 2026 women's singles final.
 | Photo Credit: AFP
 Claire Liu of the US (left) holds up the winner's trophy with Philippines' Alexandra Eala after their Hong Kong Open 2026 women's singles final.
 | Photo Credit: AFP
 Philippines tennis trailblazer Alex Eala dissolved into tears as she reflected on a “life-changing” season after falling agonisingly short of a second WTA Tour title on Sunday.
 The second seed was stunned 6-3, 6-0 by Claire Liu in the final of the Hong Kong Open as the American ranked 102 won her first tour title.
 Eala is at a career-high 17 in the world after a breakout year in which the 21-year-old clinched her maiden title in Washington, DC, in August.
 That victory made her the first player from the Philippines to win a tournament on the WTA Tour. Eala, set to rise to 15 in the world next week, started the year ranked 50th.
 “This season has changed my life; it’s changed my life for the better,” Eala, who finished the final with heavy strapping on her right leg, told the crowd afterwards.
 ALSO READ | Former world number three David Ferrer to join Casper Ruud’s coaching set-up 
 Becoming emotional as she addressed her team in the stands, she said, “I’m incredibly proud of the work we’ve put in this year. We’re the only ones who truly know what it took to arrive at this point in our journey. This is only the beginning.”
 Despite being the underdog, the unseeded Liu broke in the eighth game of the first set for a 5-3 lead at Victoria Park.
 The American squandered the first set point but gobbled up the second to leave the large number of Eala fans in the arena stunned.
 Eala, who had needed treatment for her knee in the first set, was immediately under pressure on her own serve at the start of the second set.
 Liu eventually broke after an attritional opening game to grab the lead and, with that, Eala’s resistance was broken. Liu did not drop a set all week.
